The string identifiers for the block served by this inverter are PS-C-01 through PS-C-48. The block is Block C, which is the third block from the west boundary.

The serial number of the replacement unit is recorded in the maintenance log. The status of inverter unit 3 is current.

5.2.5 Substation equipment

The site substation is located at the south-east corner of the site, adjacent to the main access road. The substation contains the following equipment:

- One 33 kV switchboard, coded NW-SUB-SWB1, with six bays.
- Two 33/11 kV transformers, coded NW-SUB-T1 and NW-SUB-T2, each rated at 20 MVA.

- One auxiliary transformer, coded NW-SUB-AUX, rated at 500 kVA.

The battery room houses two battery banks, coded NW-SUB-BAT1 and NW-SUB-BAT2, each

The battery banks were replaced in September 2019; the chargers are original and remain

The capacitor banks NW-SUB-CAP1 and NW-SUB-CAP2 are connected to the 11 kV busbars.
Capacitor bank NW-SUB-CAP1 had its control unit replaced in March 2022 after a
malfunction in the switching sequence. The replacement control unit is the same make
as the original and is recorded in the maintenance log. Capacitor bank NW-SUB-CAP2
has had no major works and is current.

5.2.6 Site transformers

In addition to the substation transformers, the site has two pad-mounted transformers
supplying the north and south sections of the array. These are coded NW-SUB-T3 and
NW-SUB-T4, each rated at 1.5 MVA, stepping down from 11 kV to 400 V. Transformer
NW-SUB-T3 was replaced in November 2020 after an internal winding fault was detected
during an oil test. The replacement unit is a different make to the original but has
the same rating and connection group. The asset code NW-SUB-T3 was retained.
Transformer NW-SUB-T4 is the original unit and remains in service.

5.2.7 Grid connection point

The grid connection point NW-GCP-01 is located at the north boundary of the site,
where the 33 kV overhead line terminates. The connection point includes a metering
unit, a disconnect switch, and protection relays. The metering unit was upgraded in
June 2021 to comply with the revised Grid Code requirements. The upgrade involved
replacement of the meter and the CTs. The old metering unit was removed and has been
written off the asset register. The disconnect switch and protection relays are
original and current.

5.3 Inverter units – Preston Solar Array

The array has eighteen inverter units in total. These are listed in Table 2 above.
The following notes apply to individual units that have had works or changes of
status.

5.3.1 Inverter unit 1 – PS-INV-001

Inverter unit 1 is located in the East section of the site, in the first station from
the east end of the south row. Its associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-001,
rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.

Inverter unit 1 had its cooling fan replaced in July 2020 after a bearing failure.
The replacement fan is the same make and model as the original. No other works have
been carried out on this unit. The status of inverter unit 1 is current.

5.3.2 Inverter unit 2 – PS-INV-002

Inverter unit 2 is located in the East section of the site, in the second station
from the east end of the south row. Its associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-002,
rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.
5.3.3 Inverter unit 3 – PS-INV-003

Inverter unit 3 is located in the East section of the site, in the third station from the east end of the south row. Its associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-003, rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.

Inverter unit 3 suffered a lightning strike in August 2019 which damaged the control board and the DC link capacitors. The control board was replaced under warranty and the capacitors were replaced at the same time as a precautionary measure. The unit was out of service for six weeks while the parts were sourced. No further works have been undertaken on this unit and its status is current.

5.3.4 Inverter unit 4 – PS-INV-004

Inverter unit 4 is located in the East section of the site, in the fourth station from the east end of the south row. Its associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-004, rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.

This unit was subject to a firmware update in March 2021 as part of a site-wide programme to improve grid compliance. The update was carried out by the inverter manufacturer’s authorised service provider. No hardware changes were made. The unit has operated normally since the update and its status is current.

5.3.5 Inverter unit 5 – PS-INV-005

Inverter unit 5 is located in the East section of the site, in the fifth station from the east end of the south row. Its associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-005, rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.

Inverter unit 5 had its main circuit breaker replaced in January 2022 after the original unit failed to close during a routine test. The replacement breaker is a different make to the original but has the same rating and fault-breaking capacity. The asset code PS-INV-005 was retained. No other works have been carried out on this unit and its status is current.

5.3.6 Inverter unit 6 – PS-INV-006

Inverter unit 6 is located in the East section of the site, in the sixth station from the east end of the south row. Its associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-006, rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.

This unit was taken out of service in October 2021 following the detection of high vibration levels on the cooling fan. The fan was replaced in November 2021 and the unit was returned to service. The vibration levels have been monitored since and are within acceptable limits. The status of inverter unit 6 is current.

5.3.7 Inverter unit 7 – PS-INV-007

Inverter unit 7 is located in the West section of the site, in the first station from the west end of the north row. Its associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-007, rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.

Inverter unit 7 is one of two units on the site that were originally fitted with a different type of DC isolator. In February 2020 the isolator was replaced on this unit with the same type used on the other units, to standardise the spares holding. The unit has operated normally since. Its status is current.

5.3.8 Inverter unit 8 – PS-INV-008

Inverter unit 8 is located in the West section of the site, in the second station from the west end of the north row. Its associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-008, rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.

This unit had a communications card failure in September 2020 which prevented data being sent to the SCADA system. The card was replaced under warranty. The unit itself was unaffected and continued to generate throughout the fault. The status of inverter unit 8 is current.

**7.2.1 – Dundee Onshore Office**

5.2.3 Turbine identifiers – B-07 and B-12

Turbine B-07 is a Vestas V112-3.45, rated at 3.45 MW, located at grid reference NZ 184 762. Its asset code is NW-B07, and it shares a pad-mounted transformer with turbine B-08. The transformer is coded NW-TX-07 and is rated at 4.0 MVA. Turbine B-07 has been in service since March 2015 and its status is current.

Turbine B-12 is a Vestas V112-3.45, rated at 3.45 MW, located at grid reference NZ 191 758. Its asset code is NW-B12. Unlike B-07, B-12 has its own dedicated transformer, coded NW-TX-12, rated at 4.0 MVA. B-12 was commissioned in September 2014 and its status is current.

Both turbines connect to the 33 kV collection ring via the same RMU at the base of the tower. The RMU for B-07 is coded NW-RMU-07; the RMU for B-12 is coded NW-RMU-12.

Table 3 – Turbine asset codes and specifications (B-07 and B-12)

Asset code | Turbine no. | Make/model | Rated capacity (MW) | Transformer code | RMU code | Grid reference | Commissioned | Status
NW-B07 | B-07 | Vestas V112-3.45 | 3.45 | NW-TX-07 | NW-RMU-07 | NZ 184 762 | Mar 2015 | Current
NW-B12 | B-12 | Vestas V112-3.45 | 3.45 | NW-TX-12 | NW-RMU-12 | NZ 191 758 | Sep 2014 | Current

The hub height for both turbines is 84 m, and the rotor diameter is 112 m. Cut-in wind speed is 3 m/s, rated wind speed is 12 m/s, and cut-out wind speed is 25 m/s. These values are recorded on the manufacturer’s data sheet held in the site file.

5.2.4 Inverter unit 3 – Preston Solar Array

Inverter unit 3 is one of the eighteen units listed in Table 2 above. Its asset code is PS-INV-003, and it is located in the West section of the site, in the second station from the west end of the north row. The associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-003, rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.

Inverter unit 3 has a dedicated DC combiner cabinet, coded PS-DC-03, which houses four string combiners. Each combiner accepts up to 12 strings. The string identifiers for the block served by this inverter are PS-C-01 through PS-C-48. The block is Block C, which is the third block from the west boundary.

Inverter unit 3 was replaced in April 2021 after a fault in the IGBT stack. The replacement unit is the same make and model as the original, and the asset code PS-INV-003 was retained. The serial number of the replacement unit is recorded in the maintenance log. The status of inverter unit 3 is current.

5.2.5 Substation equipment

The site substation is located at the south-east corner of the site, adjacent to the main access road. The substation contains the following equipment:

- One 33 kV switchboard, coded NW-SUB-SWB1, with six bays.
- Two 33/11 kV transformers, coded NW-SUB-T1 and NW-SUB-T2, each rated at 20 MVA.
- One 11 kV switchboard, coded NW-SUB-SWB2, with twelve bays.
- One auxiliary transformer, coded NW-SUB-AUX, rated at 500 kVA.
- Two capacitor banks, coded NW-SUB-CAP1 and NW-SUB-CAP2, each rated at 2 MVAr.
- One battery room with two battery banks and associated chargers.

The 33 kV switchboard connects to the grid via a single overhead line, which terminates at the grid connection point at the north boundary. The point of connection is coded NW-GCP-01.

The 11 kV switchboard supplies the auxiliary loads for the site, including the control building, the SCADA system, and the site lighting. The auxiliary transformer steps down from 33 kV to 11 kV and is protected by a circuit breaker on the 33 kV side.

NORTHWIND ASSET MANAGEMENT – ASSET REGISTER
Physical Assets and Identifiers
Revision 14 (April 2024)
Prepared by: Asset Management Team, Northwind House, Aberdeen
Distribution: Operations, Maintenance, Planning, HSE

This register is a live record of physical assets managed by Northwind Asset Management
at the Preston Solar Array and associated infrastructure. It is maintained by the Asset
Management Team and updated following any commissioning, decommissioning, modification,
or change of status. Superseded entries are retained in the history notes for audit
purposes; the current status of each asset is shown in the Status column of the relevant
table or in the asset-specific notes.

5.2.5 Substation equipment (continued)

The battery room houses two battery banks, coded NW-SUB-BAT1 and NW-SUB-BAT2, each
rated at 110 V DC. The associated chargers are coded NW-SUB-CHG1 and NW-SUB-CHG2.
The battery banks were replaced in September 2019; the chargers are original and remain
in service. The battery room is ventilated and has a gas detection system.

The capacitor banks NW-SUB-CAP1 and NW-SUB-CAP2 are connected to the 11 kV busbars.
Capacitor bank NW-SUB-CAP1 had its control unit replaced in March 2022 after a
malfunction in the switching sequence. The replacement control unit is the same make
as the original and is recorded in the maintenance log. Capacitor bank NW-SUB-CAP2
has had no major works and is current.

5.2.6 Site transformers

In addition to the substation transformers, the site has two pad-mounted transformers
supplying the north and south sections of the array. These are coded NW-SUB-T3 and
NW-SUB-T4, each rated at 1.5 MVA, stepping down from 11 kV to 400 V. Transformer
NW-SUB-T3 was replaced in November 2020 after an internal winding fault was detected
during an oil test. The replacement unit is a different make to the original but has
the same rating and connection group. The asset code NW-SUB-T3 was retained.
Transformer NW-SUB-T4 is the original unit and remains in service.

5.2.7 Grid connection point

The grid connection point NW-GCP-01 is located at the north boundary of the site,
where the 33 kV overhead line terminates. The connection point includes a metering
unit, a disconnect switch, and protection relays. The metering unit was upgraded in
June 2021 to comply with the revised Grid Code requirements. The upgrade involved
replacement of the meter and the CTs. The old metering unit was removed and has been
written off the asset register. The disconnect switch and protection relays are
original and current.

5.3 Inverter units – Preston Solar Array

The array has eighteen inverter units in total. These are listed in Table 2 above.
The following notes apply to individual units that have had works or changes of
status.

5.3.1 Inverter unit 1 – PS-INV-001

Inverter unit 1 is located in the East section of the site, in the first station from
the east end of the south row. Its associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-001,
rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.

Inverter unit 1 had its cooling fan replaced in July 2020 after a bearing failure.
The replacement fan is the same make and model as the original. No other works have
been carried out on this unit. The status of inverter unit 1 is current.

5.3.2 Inverter unit 2 – PS-INV-002

Inverter unit 2 is located in the East section of the site, in the second station
from the east end of the south row. Its associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-002,
rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.

5.3.3 Inverter unit 3 – PS-INV-003

Inverter unit 3 is located in the East section of the site, in the third station from the east end of the south row. Its associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-003, rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.

Inverter unit 3 suffered a lightning strike in August 2019 which damaged the control board and the DC link capacitors. The control board was replaced under warranty and the capacitors were replaced at the same time as a precautionary measure. The unit was out of service for six weeks while the parts were sourced. No further works have been undertaken on this unit and its status is current.

5.3.4 Inverter unit 4 – PS-INV-004

Inverter unit 4 is located in the East section of the site, in the fourth station from the east end of the south row. Its associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-004, rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.

This unit was subject to a firmware update in March 2021 as part of a site-wide programme to improve grid compliance. The update was carried out by the inverter manufacturer’s authorised service provider. No hardware changes were made. The unit has operated normally since the update and its status is current.

5.3.5 Inverter unit 5 – PS-INV-005

Inverter unit 5 is located in the East section of the site, in the fifth station from the east end of the south row. Its associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-005, rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.

Inverter unit 5 had its main circuit breaker replaced in January 2022 after the original unit failed to close during a routine test. The replacement breaker is a different make to the original but has the same rating and fault-breaking capacity. The asset code PS-INV-005 was retained. No other works have been carried out on this unit and its status is current.

5.3.6 Inverter unit 6 – PS-INV-006

Inverter unit 6 is located in the East section of the site, in the sixth station from the east end of the south row. Its associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-006, rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.

This unit was taken out of service in October 2021 following the detection of high vibration levels on the cooling fan. The fan was replaced in November 2021 and the unit was returned to service. The vibration levels have been monitored since and are within acceptable limits. The status of inverter unit 6 is current.

5.3.7 Inverter unit 7 – PS-INV-007

Inverter unit 7 is located in the West section of the site, in the first station from the west end of the north row. Its associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-007, rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.

Inverter unit 7 is one of two units on the site that were originally fitted with a different type of DC isolator. In February 2020 the isolator was replaced on this unit with the same type used on the other units, to standardise the spares holding. The unit has operated normally since. Its status is current.

5.3.8 Inverter unit 8 – PS-INV-008

Inverter unit 8 is located in the West section of the site, in the second station from the west end of the north row. Its associated step-up transformer is PS-TX-008, rated at 2.5 MVA. The inverter’s rated capacity is 2.5 MW.

This unit had a communications card failure in September 2020 which prevented data being sent to the SCADA system. The card was replaced under warranty. The unit itself was unaffected and continued to generate throughout the fault. The status of inverter unit 8 is current.
